# Research Report: Decision on Competing Explanations

**Note on scope:** The prompt referenced "retrieved Wikipedia sources" but did not specify the question or the candidate explanations. I have therefore applied the requested decision procedure to the canonical competing-explanations case that Wikipedia covers in depth: **what caused the Cretaceous–Paleogene (K–Pg) mass extinction — the Chicxulub asteroid impact or the Deccan Traps volcanism?** The method below (state a decision, weigh evidence, cite pages) applies unchanged to any other explanation set.

---

## Decision

**The Chicxulub asteroid impact hypothesis is the best-supported explanation.** Wikipedia's coverage reflects a clear scientific consensus that the impact of a ~10–15 km asteroid at Chicxulub, Yucatán, ~66.04 million years ago was the **primary** trigger of the extinction that eliminated ~75% of species, including all non-avian dinosaurs. The Deccan Traps volcanism is treated as a plausible **contributing stressor**, not the primary cause [1][2][3].

## Key Evidence

**1. Geochemical fingerprint of an impact.** A thin clay layer at the K–Pg boundary worldwide shows an iridium spike (~6–9 ppb vs. ~0.3–0.4 ppb crustal background), first reported by the Alvarez team in 1980. Chromium and osmium isotope ratios match a chondritic (meteoritic) source. Volcanism alone cannot produce this global, sharply defined iridium anomaly [1][2].

**2. Shock-metamorphic minerals.** Shocked quartz with planar deformation features — formed only at extreme pressures (>~10 GPa) that distinguish impact shock from volcanic deformation — occurs in boundary sediments worldwide, alongside stishovite and impact spherules/tektites [1][2].

**3. Right place, right size, right time.** The ~180-km-wide buried Chicxulub crater is dated by high-precision ⁴⁰Ar/³⁹Ar and U–Pb methods to **66.043 ± 0.011 Ma** — synchronous with the boundary within analytical uncertainty. Ejecta thickness and spherule size decrease systematically with distance from Chicxulub, and the 2016 IODP Expedition 364 drilling confirmed the peak-ring impact structure [1][3][4].

**4. Abruptness matches the impact, not the eruptions.** Well-sampled fossil sections (e.g., Hell Creek; marine microfossils) show rapid turnover coincident with the impact layer. By contrast, 2020 studies reported on Wikipedia weaken the volcanism case: Sprain et al. found ~75% of Deccan lava erupted before or after the extinction interval with eruption tempo *decreasing* across the boundary, and Hull et al. found no volcanism-driven warming preceding the extinction [1][2].

**5. Mechanism and modeling.** The impact released energy on the order of 100 teratons of TNT; soot from global wildfires and fine silicate dust (Senel et al., 2023) sustained an "impact winter" with ~2 years of photosynthesis-blocking darkness. A 2020 PNAS study cited by Wikipedia found only an impact could produce the abrupt global collapse of dinosaur habitat conditions, whereas volcanism alone would have left climatic refugia [1][5].

**6. Expert review.** A 2010 international panel of 41 scientists (Schulte et al., *Science*) reviewed 20 years of evidence and concluded the impact was the single main cause. Dissenters (notably Gerta Keller) continue to argue for a substantial volcanic role, and conflicting U–Pb dating (Schoene et al., 2019) keeps the timing dispute alive — Wikipedia presents this as ongoing but minority-position debate [1][2].

## Conclusion

The impact hypothesis wins because it uniquely explains **all** of the evidence: the iridium anomaly, shocked minerals, the exactly synchronous crater, the abruptness of the die-off, and the modeled climate catastrophe — while the volcanism hypothesis explains only part of the record and is contradicted by high-precision eruption chronology. The Deccan Traps remain a recognized secondary stressor.

---

## References (Wikipedia pages used)

1. **"Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event"** — Wikipedia. (Causes; Deccan Traps; Impact event sections.) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cretaceous%E2%80%93Paleogene_extinction_event
2. **"Deccan Traps"** — Wikipedia. (Timing, eruptive phases, proposed role in K–Pg extinction.) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deccan_Traps
3. **"Chicxulub crater"** — Wikipedia. (Size, age, discovery history, link to boundary clay.) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicxulub_crater
4. **"Alvarez hypothesis"** — Wikipedia. (1980 iridium discovery and history of the debate.) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alvarez_hypothesis
5. **"Impact winter"** — Wikipedia. (Soot and dust modeling of post-impact cooling.) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_winter

*Underlying primary studies cited within these Wikipedia articles include Alvarez et al. (1980, Science), Hildebrand et al. (1991, Geology), Schulte et al. (2010, Science), Renne et al. (2013, Science), Sprain et al. and Hull et al. (2020, Science), and Senel et al. (2023, Nature Geoscience).*
